articles.title: How an AI Support Agent Learns From Agent Edits
articles.excerpt: Every time a support agent edits an AI draft before sending it, they show the system how the company actually handles that case. In the 30 days to 19 November 2026, agents in the deployment from our c…
articles.body: Every time a support agent edits an AI draft before sending it, they show the system how the company actually handles that case. In the 30 days to 19 November 2026, agents in the deployment from our case study edited 19,339 AI drafts. That is the most valuable training material the system has, and it is easy to lose. This is the loop we built to use it, and what it found. Keep both versions The loop needs two texts for every reply: what the AI drafted and what was sent. Many systems store one reply field, and the agent's edit overwrites the draft. From that day nobody can tell what the AI wrote. The AI's draft is stored in its own field and never overwritten. Before trusting any comparison, test it on replies the AI sent with no person involved.

articles.title: Building a WhatsApp AI assistant for Moroccan businesses (Darija) with Next.js, Supabase and Claude
articles.excerpt: Most small businesses in Morocco take orders on WhatsApp. The owner reads every message, types the menu again and again, and misses messages at night. I wanted to see how far a small, cheap AI assista…
articles.body: Most small businesses in Morocco take orders on WhatsApp. The owner reads every message, types the menu again and again, and misses messages at night. I wanted to see how far a small, cheap AI assistant could go for them, so I built one that answers in Moroccan Darija, French or Arabic. The problem Customers write in Darija (often in Latin letters), French, or a mix of both. Answers must come only from the business's real menu, prices and hours. No invented dishes. The owner must be alerted when someone orders or asks for a human. One codebase has to serve many merchants without mixing their data. Architecture Routing by phone_number_id. The WhatsApp Cloud API sends every message to one webhook. The webhook finds the merchant (tenant) by the phone number ID of the receiving number.
articles.author: lamaizi hajar

articles.title: Human-in-the-Loop AI Agents: Who Approves What
articles.excerpt: "Human in the loop" is easy to say and easy to get wrong. Put the person on every step and the AI saves nobody any time. Put the person nowhere and the first wrong refund lands on your bank statement.…
articles.body: "Human in the loop" is easy to say and easy to get wrong. Put the person on every step and the AI saves nobody any time. Put the person nowhere and the first wrong refund lands on your bank statement. The useful question is narrower: which decisions does a person own, and what does the AI hand them at that moment? This is how we split it on a live customer service system that handled 36,294 customer emails and 15,445 chat conversations in the last 30 days. Draw the line at consequences, not at difficulty Teams often hand the "easy" questions to the AI and keep the "hard" ones for people. That is the wrong axis. A hard troubleshooting question with ten steps is safe for the AI to answer, because a wrong step costs the customer one more message.

articles.excerpt: I'm Dejan. I built a free seating chart maker and I want to be upfront about that. This post is about why I kept the guest list in the browser, and how the tool actually works. Wedding and event seati…
articles.body: I'm Dejan. I built a free seating chart maker and I want to be upfront about that. This post is about why I kept the guest list in the browser, and how the tool actually works. Wedding and event seating is a messy puzzle: couples who should stay together, relatives who should not sit at the same table, meal counts for the caterer, and a floor plan you can print. Most tools I looked at want an account, or they upload the list to a server. I didn't want a guest list leaving the device at all. The tool is here: https://dejoski.github.io/seating-chart-maker/ It runs in the browser. There is no sign-up, no ads, and no guest limit. The list is stored only in the browser's local storage on that device and is never uploaded. If you need the chart on another device, use Backup (.json) and Restore.

It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. articles.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
articles.excerpt: The longest total solar eclipse on land this century promises to be the experience of a lifetime, but watching it from Luxor, Egypt, may not be straightforward. What could go wrong? Quite a lot, actua…
articles.body: On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 22 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate .
